definitions.meaning: a part-time judge in English courts is given this title
a wooden wind instrument played by blowing into the end, common in school music lessons

explanation.surface: A question about what sort of legal instrument something is.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Judicial type of instrument' reads as a legal document; split it after 'type' and read 'of' as a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses share one word: a part-time judge in Britain and an end-blown wooden flute.

clue.text: Exotic transport puts strain on author

parts.note: to rick is to sprain or wrench a joint
George Bernard Shaw, the Irish playwright

explanation.surface: Riding an unusual vehicle puts stress on a writer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Exotic' tells the solver the vehicle belongs to faraway places such as India or Japan; 'puts ... on' is the joining instruction, and 'author' is the dramatist George Bernard.
explanation.definitionFit: A rickshaw is a light hooded two-wheeled cart pulled by a runner, associated with Asia.

clue.text: Pascal concerned with the length of this "needlewoman's" nose

definitions.text: Pascal concerned with the length of this "needlewoman's" nose

parts.words: Pascal concerned with the length of this "needlewoman's" nose
parts.note: Pascal remarked that had a certain Egyptian queen's nose been shorter, the face of the world would have changed; the London obelisk bears her name with 'Needle'

explanation.walkthrough: Blaise Pascal's Pensées speculates on history turning on the Egyptian queen's nose; 'needlewoman' alludes to the Thames obelisk named Cleopatra's Needle.
explanation.definitionFit: The last Ptolemaic queen of Egypt, famed for beauty and for the needle-shaped obelisk named after her.

clue.text: Lover makes rings round me? Right first time

indicators.note: says this piece is put at the very start

parts.note: rings are round shapes like the letter O, two of them

explanation.surface: A suitor asks if he's circling the speaker, getting it right at once.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rings round me' puts O and O either side of ME; 'first time' puts R at the front.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's young romantic hero gives his name to any ardent male suitor.

clue.text: Letter gives record on Agave fibre

indicators.note: in a down clue, on means placed after the other piece

parts.note: EP is an extended-play record
istle is a fibre from agave plants used for cord and brushes

explanation.surface: A letter delivers a record made from plant fibre.
explanation.definitionFit: An epistle is a formal letter, as in the New Testament epistles.

parts.note: Kate is the title character of Shakespeare's The Taming of the Shrew
D is the usual abbreviation for died in genealogies

explanation.surface: Shakespeare's Kate, having died, knows something.
explanation.walkthrough: Kate is Katherina in Shakespeare's comedy The Taming of the Shrew, so she stands for SHREW; 'this' just points back to the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Being shrewd means having sharp judgement, being astute and worldly-wise.

clue.text: Volunteers like sentry at Buckingham Palace?

definitions.meaning: the British wartime civilian defence force of volunteers
a soldier guarding the monarch's home is literally guarding a home

explanation.surface: Volunteers resembling the sentries outside the royal palace.
explanation.walkthrough: The British Home Guard was the volunteer defence force of World War II; a palace sentry literally guards a home.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses: the WWII British local defence volunteers, and a literal guard posted at a residence.

clue.text: Set up limits of court before starting

indicators.note: says this piece comes at the start

parts.note: ere is an old word for before

indicators.note: the limits of a word are its first and last letters

explanation.surface: Build up the edges of a court before beginning.
explanation.definitionFit: To erect is to build or raise something upright, to put up.

clue.text: "Men love in haste, but they — at leisure" (Byron)

definitions.text: "Men love in haste, but they — at leisure" (Byron)

parts.words: "Men love in haste, but they — at leisure" (Byron)
parts.note: the missing word in this line from Byron's Don Juan is the verb meaning loathe, set against love

explanation.walkthrough: A fill-in-the-blank quotation from Byron's Don Juan; the missing verb is the opposite of 'love'.
explanation.definitionFit: The gap needs the opposite of loving: to loathe or hate intensely.

clue.text: Makes one's' mark with orchestral works

definitions.meaning: cuts or scratches lines into something
written music for an orchestra

explanation.surface: Someone makes an impression with symphonies.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses: verb for scratching lines or marks, and the written sheet music of orchestral pieces.

clue.text: Study hard consuming energy, that's the best

indicators.note: one word eating another means the second goes inside the first

parts.note: to cram is to study intensively, usually just before an exam
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Swotting with great effort is the finest approach.
explanation.definitionFit: The cream is the choicest part of anything, as in 'the cream of the crop'.

indicators.note: says the words that come before are to be taken as spoken, matching a word of different spelling

parts.note: a stipend is an income, and dishonest is bent, giving income bent

explanation.surface: Is a vicar's salary crooked?
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of 'Clergyman's' stands for 'is'; 'income bent' spoken quickly matches the answer's sound. 'Bent' is British slang for dishonest or corrupt.
explanation.definitionFit: A Church of England parish priest holding a benefice is formally called by this title.

clue.text: The lion or unicorn as a football fan

definitions.meaning: in heraldry the figures standing either side of a shield, like the lion and unicorn of the royal arms, have this name
a follower of a team

explanation.surface: Is the lion or the unicorn on the royal arms a football follower?
explanation.walkthrough: The lion and the unicorn hold up the shield on the British royal coat of arms, which makes them heraldic figures of this kind.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses: heraldic figures that hold up a shield, and a fan who backs a club.

indicators.note: out signals the following word is jumbled into a new order

explanation.surface: Exits leading off the theatre stage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ways out' looks like the definition, meaning exits; only 'Ways' defines, and 'out' rearranges STAGE, with 'from the' as link words.
explanation.definitionFit: Gates are openings through which one passes, so they are ways in or out.

parts.note: an is the indefinite article in grammar

indicators.note: says the next word could be something else once rearranged

explanation.surface: A newspaper article might be rather dated.
explanation.definitionFit: Something antique is aged and from an earlier era, especially collectable furniture.

definitions.meaning: a builder's price given in advance
a passage valued and repeated from a book

explanation.surface: Assessing what a piece of writing is worth.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses: a priced estimate for work, and a passage repeated from a written text.

clue.text: Ghost seen to perform in small wood

indicators.note: one piece sits within another piece

parts.note: shaw is an old word for a thicket or small wood
to do is to perform

explanation.surface: A ghost is spotted acting in a copse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Seen to' is a link; SHAW, a poetic word for a copse, holds DO.
explanation.definitionFit: A shadow is a faint phantom or spectre, a shade of the departed.

definitions.meaning: a seller of clothes and equipment
someone who has just left a health spa is out and in better shape

explanation.surface: A tradesman departing from a spa.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading splits the answer into OUT and FITTER: a guest emerging from a health farm in better shape.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses: a clothing merchant, and a person out of a health spa and in better condition.

definitions.meaning: dragging, scraping footwork in a dance
mixing up playing cards of all suits

explanation.surface: Dance moves that unsettle the clubs.
explanation.walkthrough: Clubs are a suit of playing cards; mixing the pack is the second meaning.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses: sliding dance steps, and mixing up a pack of cards before dealing.

clue.text: Show displeasure in bar — the monkey!

indicators.note: one piece is placed inside another piece

parts.note: to bar is to ban
to boo is to jeer and show displeasure

explanation.surface: Someone jeering in a pub, scolding a monkey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bar' looks like a pub, but it is a verb meaning prohibit.
explanation.definitionFit: A baboon is a large ground-dwelling African primate with a dog-like muzzle.

clue.text: Doze with family paper perhaps at table

parts.note: a nap is a short sleep
kin are relatives

explanation.surface: Dozing with relatives, with a newspaper at dinner.
explanation.definitionFit: A serviette, which may be made of paper, is used at meals to wipe the mouth.

parts.note: an old command 'hence!' means go away
'old Dutch' is Cockney slang for a wife

explanation.surface: Therefore a wife would split the bill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hence' looks like 'therefore', but in old usage it is a command to depart. 'My old Dutch' is London Cockney slang for one's wife.
explanation.definitionFit: To go Dutch is the idiom for each diner paying their own share of a meal.

clue.text: Grenade thrown by one of high rank

indicators.note: letters thrown about land in a new order

explanation.surface: A grenade hurled by a nobleman.
explanation.definitionFit: A grandee is a Spanish nobleman of the highest rank, or any eminent person.

definitions.meaning: a black-and-white member of the crow family
in target shooting, a hit in the second ring from the outside, scoring poorly

explanation.surface: A bird clumsily brought down.
explanation.walkthrough: In rifle shooting a shot striking the outer ring but one of the target goes by this bird's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses: the chattering black-and-white crow, and a poor shot on a target.

indicators.note: a military manoeuvre moves things around, signalling the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Troops manoeuvre close to a battlefield.
explanation.definitionFit: An arena is a scene of conflict or contest, figuratively any field of battle.

definitions.meaning: to write down in a register or ledger
the script's instruction for an actor to come on

explanation.surface: Write down a director's instruction.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses: to log an item in a book, and the script's cue for an actor to come on.

parts.note: plain means simple or unadorned
a tiff is a minor squabble

explanation.surface: A simple squabble with a toy soldier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Action man' suggests the toy soldier; here it means one who brings a legal action.
explanation.definitionFit: A plaintiff is the person who brings a lawsuit, starting legal proceedings.

definitions.meaning: banknotes are paper money
the answer to 9 down is music scores, which are written in musical symbols

explanation.surface: Perhaps cash within the scores.
explanation.walkthrough: '9' points to 9 down, orchestral scores, which are made up of musical symbols.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses: paper money such as banknotes, and the written symbols of music.

parts.note: a word for terrified that also describes, literally, what the Gorgon's gaze did, turning victims to stone

explanation.definitionFit: Petrified means terrified, and literally turned to stone, as Medusa's gaze did to onlookers.

definitions.meaning: a sum or whole amount
the figure written at the foot of an added column of numbers

explanation.surface: Aggregate stone at the foot of a pillar.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses: the overall sum, and the figure written beneath an added-up column of figures.

parts.note: to err is to sin or go wrong

explanation.surface: Do wrong and be given a job.
explanation.definitionFit: A commission in the sense of a task one is sent to carry out for someone.

definitions.meaning: gauges how big or long something is
actions or moves made to achieve an end

explanation.surface: Someone checks how far the steps go.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses: verb for sizing something up, and noun for actions or provisions put into effect.
